title: Replace DateTime.now() with a fixed clock value in scheduler test fixture seeding
why: TQ-6 requires hermetic tests with no wall-clock. All three files otherwise correctly drive their actual scheduling assertions off a fixed `DateTime.utc(...)` 'now'/'today' constant — but the CurriculumTracksCompanion.insert(...) calls that seed the track row use the real system clock for stateChangedAt/activatedAt instead of that same fixed constant. No current assertion reads these two columns, so it doesn't flip any test's pass/fail today, but it's an easy trap: the moment a future test (or the production code these tests exercise) starts reading track state-change recency, these three tests will intermittently disagree with their own fixed 'now' by however many days/years separate the two clocks.
recommendation: Pass the file's existing fixed now/today constant for stateChangedAt/activatedAt instead of DateTime.now(), matching the pattern already used for every other timestamp in the same setUp blocks.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -n 'DateTime.now()'` across the three files returns nothing.
